newsitem.title: INDIA: India L&T to build Rs.15 bln technopark.
newsitem.headline: India L&T to build Rs.15 bln technopark.

text.p: Indian engineering and construction firm Larsen & Toubro said on Saturday it signed an agreement with the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructural Corp (APIIC) to build a 15 billion rupee technopark in the southern city of Hyderabad.
"It would be a joint venture of L&T and APIIC, the former holding 89 percent of the equity in the new venture," he said.
The first phase, to be completed within two years of commencement, will involve an outlay of 800 million rupees.

"The technopark will seek to attract potential industries in the areas of computer software, hardware, electronics, engineering and design organisations, banking and other service related companies and offer them office space with state-of-art facilities for modern functioning," L&T said in a statement.
L&T and its associate companies will build the park and provide communication and other services.
The park will contain residential accommodation, recreation centres, showrooms, conference facilities, restaurants, banking facilities, shopping complexes and captive power plant, it said.
The project is expected to cover about six million square feet of built up area.
Andhra Pradesh chief minister Chandrababu Naidu told reporters after the signing ceremony he expected 50 billion rupees in annual business on completion of the project.
The APIIC is primarily investing by way of land cost while the rest of the investment will come from L&T, he said.

The existing Hyderabad Software Technology Park will move into the proposed park, J.A.Chowdary, its head said. "The same incentives which are available to entrepreneurs at the present park will be available to them at the new city," he said.
